big_picture_notes: Philippians is a personal, joy‑suffused letter whose leitmotif of joy/rejoicing forms an inclusio across the whole (1:18, 26; 2:17–18; 3:1; 4:1, 4, 10). The Christ‑Hymn (2:5–11) is the theological/ethical hinge: Paul’s circumstances → exhortation (1:12–2:4), grounded in Christ’s example (2:5–11), then applied (2:12–30), followed by polemical warning and pursuit of Christ (ch. 3), and practical instruction/thanks (ch. 4). A sharp rhetorical turn at 3:2 re‑engages urgency. Glue: partnership (koinōnia), unity/humility, and imitation.

stories.story_title: The Foundation of Joy: Salutation and the Example of Suffering
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (1:1) epistolary salutation; end (2:4) completes the unity/humility exhortation before shifting to the Christ‑Hymn (2:5). Glue: koinōnia in the gospel, joy language, and the parallel of Paul’s chains with the Philippians’ call to stand and suffer (1:27–30).

scenes.scene_name: Salutation
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ, greet the saints, overseers, and deacons at Philippi.

scenes.scene_name: Thanksgiving: Confident of His Good Work
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Joyful thanks for their partnership, sure that He who began a good work will complete it.

scenes.scene_name: Prayer for Love and Discernment
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer that their love abound in knowledge and discernment, filled with the fruit of righteousness.

scenes.scene_name: Imprisonment Advances the Gospel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul's chains have emboldened the brothers and made Christ known throughout the praetorium.

scenes.scene_name: Christ Preached, Whether in Pretense or Truth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Some preach from envy, some from love — but Paul rejoices that Christ is proclaimed either way.

scenes.scene_name: To Live Is Christ, to Die Is Gain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confident of deliverance, Paul's earnest hope that Christ be exalted whether by life or death.

scenes.scene_name: Torn Between the Two; Remaining for Their Progress
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Hard-pressed between departing to be with Christ and remaining for their progress and joy in the faith.

scenes.scene_name: Live Worthy: Unity and Humility
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: ‘Only let your manner of life…’ through ‘look to others’ interests’; completes the initial paraenesis. Devices: stand/strive/suffer triad, humility antitheses, unity focus.

stories.story_title: Christ’s Humiliation and Ministers Who Embody It
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (2:5) introduces the paradigm: ‘Have this mind… in Christ Jesus’; end (3:1) ‘Finally… rejoice’ closes the humility/examples unit before the abrupt polemic in 3:2. Glue: kenosis→exaltation pattern echoed in Paul, Timothy, Epaphroditus; shared service/leitourgia.

scenes.scene_name: Christ Emptied Himself, Obedient to Death
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The hymn: Christ, in the form of God, humbled Himself to death on a cross.

scenes.scene_name: Therefore God Exalted Him; Every Knee Shall Bow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God exalted Him and gave the name above all, that every knee bow and tongue confess Him Lord.

scenes.scene_name: Work Out Your Salvation; Shine as Lights
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Work out salvation with reverence as God works in you; shine as lights without grumbling.

scenes.scene_name: Holding Fast the Word; Poured Out as an Offering
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Holding fast the word of life; Paul glad to be poured out as a drink offering for their faith.

scenes.scene_name: Timothy, a Proven Son in the Gospel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Timothy, of proven worth and genuine concern, to be sent soon with news.

scenes.scene_name: Epaphroditus, Risking His Life for the Work
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Epaphroditus sent back, who nearly died for the work of Christ — honor such men.

scenes.scene_name: Finally, Rejoice in the Lord
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The hinge: 'rejoice in the Lord' and the safeguard of repeating the same things.

stories.story_title: The Pursuit of Christ and Heavenly Citizenship
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (3:2) abrupt polemic ‘look out for the dogs’; end (4:1) stand‑firm inclusio concluding the pursuit/citizenship argument. Glue: loss/gain accounting, righteousness by faith vs flesh, imitation vs enemies of the cross, earthly vs heavenly focus.

scenes.scene_name: Beware the Dogs; Paul’s Credentials
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Triple warning; true circumcision; Paul’s blameless credentials. Devices: invective, identity contrast, autobiographical list.

scenes.scene_name: All Loss to Gain Christ
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Accounting metaphor shifts gain→loss for Christ; goal of resurrection. Devices: parallel aims (gain, be found, know), righteousness by faith.

scenes.scene_name: Pressing Toward the Goal
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Not yet attained; press on; let the mature think this way. Devices: athletic pursuit imagery, mindset exhortation.

scenes.scene_name: Imitate; Our Citizenship is in Heaven
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Imitate us vs enemies of the cross; await Savior who transforms us; ‘stand firm thus’. Devices: contrast destiny, politeuma motif, affectionate inclusio.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (4:2) direct appeals to individuals mark the concluding practical unit; end (4:23) benediction closes the epistle. Glue: peace of God/ God of peace inclusio (4:7, 9), contentment and partnership language, rejoice refrain.

scenes.scene_name: Agree in the Lord; Rejoice, the Lord Is Near
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Euodia and Syntyche urged to agree; rejoice always, for the Lord is near.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Be Anxious; The Peace of God Guards You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Replace anxiety with prayer; dwell on what is true and lovely, and the God of peace will be with you.

scenes.scene_name: Content in Every Circumstance
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul rejoices at their renewed care, having learned contentment in plenty and want, strengthened by Christ.

scenes.scene_name: The Philippians Gift; My God Will Supply
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Their generous gift a fragrant offering; and his God will supply their every need in glory.

scenes.scene_name: Final Greetings and Grace
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Greetings from the saints, especially Caesar's household, and the closing grace.
